proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \((G,T,e)\in\mathcal G_{n,k}\) and suppose that \(d_e(G)<\infty\). By the definition of \(d_e\), the element \(\lambda_e\) is algebraic over \(K_G\). The already established theorem \(\mathrm{thm:incidence\mbox{-}localization}\) identifies the fraction field of \(A_K\) with \(L\). Moreover, multiplying the covariance identity on the left by \((I_n-\Lambda)^{\mathsf T}\) and on the right by \(I_n-\Lambda\) gives
\[
\Omega=(I_n-\Lambda)^{\mathsf T}\Sigma(I_n-\Lambda).
\]
Thus every coordinate of \(\Omega\) belongs to \(K_G(\lambda_D)\), while the reverse containment follows from \(K_G\subseteq L\) and \(\lambda_D\subseteq L\). Hence
\[
L=K_G(\lambda_D).
\]

Choose a subset \(U\subseteq\lambda_D\setminus\{\lambda_e\}\) maximal algebraically independent over \(K_G\), put \(F=K_G(U)\), and let
\[
y=(y_1,\ldots,y_q)=\lambda_D\setminus U,
\qquad q=|D|-|U|.
\]
Maximality of \(U\), together with algebraicity of \(\lambda_e\) over \(K_G\), shows that every coordinate in \(y\) is algebraic over \(F\). Therefore \(L=F(y)\) is finite over \(F\); it is separable because all fields have characteristic zero. If \(p(t)\in K_G[t]\) is the minimal polynomial of \(\lambda_e\), Gauss's lemma applied to the purely transcendental extension \(K_G(U)/K_G\) shows that \(p\) remains irreducible in \(F[t]\). Consequently
\[
[F(\lambda_e):F]=[K_G(\lambda_e):K_G]=d_e(G).
\]

Localize the incidence presentation first at \(S_G\) and then at the nonzero elements of \(K_G[U]\). The resulting evaluation map
\[
F[y_1,\ldots,y_q]\longrightarrow L
\]
has kernel generated by the missing-bidirected residuals \(F_{ij}\). For each \(a\in\{1,\ldots,q\}\), let \(g_a(t)\in F[t]\) be the minimal polynomial of \(y_a\). Then \(g_a(y_a)\) lies in that kernel and can be written as an \(F[y]\)-linear combination of the residuals. Differentiating this identity and evaluating in \(L\) eliminates the terms multiplied by residuals. Since separability gives \(g_a'(y_a)\neq0\), the evaluated residual gradients span every coordinate covector \(dy_a\). Hence the residual Jacobian with respect to \(y\) has rank \(q\) over \(L\). Select residuals \(f_1,\ldots,f_q\) whose \(q\)-by-\(q\) Jacobian determinant \(\Delta\) is nonzero in \(L\).

There are exactly \(d_e(G)\) distinct \(F\)-embeddings of \(F(\lambda_e)\) into an algebraic closure \(\overline F\). Each extends to an \(F\)-embedding of \(L\): adjoining finitely many algebraic generators one at a time, an embedding extends at each step by sending the next generator to a root in \(\overline F\) of the transported minimal polynomial. Every extension sends \(f_1=\cdots=f_q=0\) to the same equations and sends \(\Delta\neq0\) to a nonzero value. Thus it yields a nonsingular isolated zero of the selected square system over \(\overline F\). Distinct embeddings of \(F(\lambda_e)\) yield distinct values of \(\lambda_e\).

Partition the variables \(y\) into their nonempty child-vertex blocks. If \(r_v\) is the size of the block at \(v\), then
\[
1\leq r_v\leq\operatorname{indeg}_D(v).
\]
By the displayed definition of \(F_{ij}\), a selected residual is affine-linear in one block when only one of its two child blocks remains in \(y\), and has block degree at most one in each of two distinct blocks otherwise. Decompose the selected square system into connected equation-block components. The nonzero determinant term inducing this decomposition matches the rows and variable columns within each component, so a component \(C\) with \(q_C\) variables also has \(q_C\) equations.

Consider the component containing \(\lambda_e\). Let \(b\) be its number of blocks, \(u\) its number of unary equations, and \(m_H\) its number of binary equations. Then
\[
q_C=u+m_H.
\]
When \(b>1\), the binary equations define a connected graph \(H\) on the \(b\) blocks. This graph is simple: a binary residual is indexed by one unordered pair of distinct child vertices, and the symmetric duplicate cannot occur in a nonzero determinant. When \(b=1\), there are no binary equations.

By \(\mathrm{lem:multihomogeneous\mbox{-}bezout\mbox{-}isolated\mbox{-}bound}\), the number of isolated zeros of this component, counted with multiplicity, is at most the coefficient of \(\prod_{v\in C}X_v^{r_v}\) in
\[
\left(\prod_{\ell=1}^{u}X_{v(\ell)}\right)
\left(\prod_{\{v,w\}\in E(H)}(X_v+X_w)\right).
\]
After the unary exponents are removed, this coefficient counts orientations of \(H\) with a prescribed indegree at every vertex: selecting \(X_v\) from the factor for \(\{v,w\}\) orients that edge toward \(v\). Fix a spanning tree of \(H\). Once the
\[
g=m_H-b+1
\]
non-tree edges have been oriented, there is at most one compatible orientation of the tree. Indeed, at a leaf the required residual indegree forces the orientation of its sole remaining tree edge, after which deleting that leaf reduces the assertion to a smaller tree. Therefore the coefficient is at most \(2^g\). For \(b=1\), the coefficient is one and we set \(g=0\).

Every distinct conjugate of \(\lambda_e\) gives a distinct isolated zero in this query component; components not containing the query cannot increase the number of queried-coordinate values. It follows that
\[
d_e(G)\leq2^g.
\]
We now bound \(g\) in two independent ways. First, if \(b>1\), simplicity of \(H\) gives
\[
g=m_H-b+1
\leq\binom b2-b+1
=\binom{b-1}{2}.
\]
The root of the supplied arborescence has no incoming directed edge: any such edge, together with the directed tree path from the root to its tail, would contradict \(\mathrm{ass:acyclic}\). Hence it contributes no child block, so \(b\leq n-1\). Therefore
\[
g\leq\binom{n-2}{2}.
\]
The same conclusion holds for \(b=1\), because then \(g=0\) and \(n\geq2\) by \(\mathrm{ass:size}\).

Second, for \(b>1\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
g
&=q_C-u-b+1\\
&\leq q_C-b+1\\
&\leq\sum_{v\in C}\bigl(\operatorname{indeg}_D(v)-1\bigr)+1\\
&\leq\sum_{v\neq\mathrm{root}}\bigl(\operatorname{indeg}_D(v)-1\bigr)+1\\
&=|D|-n+2.
\end{aligned}
\]
The penultimate inequality uses the arborescence edge entering every nonroot vertex, so each omitted summand is nonnegative. For \(b=1\), \(g=0\leq |D|-n+2\), because \(T\subseteq D\) and \(|T|=n-1\). Combining the two bounds on \(g\) proves
\[
d_e(G)\leq2^{\min\{|D|-n+2,\binom{n-2}{2}\}}.
\]
Finally, \(|T|=n-1\) and \(T\subseteq D\), so
\[
|D|-n+2=|D\setminus T|+1\leq k+1
\]
by \(\mathrm{ass:excess\mbox{-}budget}\). Monotonicity of the minimum and of \(x\mapsto2^x\) yields
\[
2^{\min\{|D|-n+2,\binom{n-2}{2}\}}
\leq2^{\min\{k+1,\binom{n-2}{2}\}},
\]
which proves the claimed size-sensitive ceiling. The argument counted only isolated zeros of the query component after freezing a transcendence basis, so it did not require the full generic parameter fiber to be zero dimensional.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For every \((G,T,e)\in\mathcal G_{n,k}\), put \(r=|D\setminus T|\). There is a universal \(C>0\) such that \(\mathsf A(G,T,e,\delta)\) returns, with total symbolic error probability at most \(\delta\), exactly one of the following four mutually exclusive outputs.
\[
\begin{array}{lll}
r=0,\ d_e(G)<\infty:
&\displaystyle
(\operatorname{tree},d_e(G),(\rho_i)_{i=1}^{d_e(G)}),
&d_e(G)\in\{1,2\},\\[3pt]
r=0,\ d_e(G)=\infty:
&(\operatorname{tree},\infty),&\\[3pt]
r>0,\ d_e(G)<\infty:
&\displaystyle
(\operatorname{algebraic},\mathcal J_{G,e},2^{\min\{|D|-n+2,\binom{n-2}{2}\}}),
&\displaystyle d_e(G)\leq2^{\min\{|D|-n+2,\binom{n-2}{2}\}}\leq2^{\min\{k+1,\binom{n-2}{2}\}},\\[3pt]
r>0,\ d_e(G)=\infty:
&(\infty,\mathcal N_{G,e}).&
\end{array}
\]
In the first case, the \(\rho_i\) are all the fractional affine square-root expressions returned by the complete tree algorithm and exhaust the generic complex queried-coordinate values. In the third case, \(\mathcal J_{G,e}\) is a Jacobian-rank transcript certifying algebraicity, but the output does not claim to compute \(d_e(G)\), \(p_e\), \(\mathcal Q_{G,e}\), or \(h_{G,e}\). In the fourth case, \(\mathcal N_{G,e}\) certifies that the queried-coordinate projection of the integral generic fiber is dominant onto \(\mathbb A^1_{K_G}\). In \(\mathsf{ArithmeticModel}\), the construction time and certificate length are at most \(n^{C(k+1)}\operatorname{poly}(\log(1/\delta))\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The positive-excess algebraic dispatcher must report the newly proved size-sensitive ceiling. Its output remains only an algebraicity transcript and an upper bound, not the exact degree or eliminant.

proposed.name: Zero-excess exact and positive-excess tag dispatcher
proposed.construction: Let \(r=|D\setminus T|\). In \(\mathsf{ArithmeticModel}\), dispatch as follows. If \(r=0\), invoke the complete published tree procedure on the equal class \(\mathcal G_{n,0}\). When \(d_e(G)<\infty\), return \((\operatorname{tree},d_e(G),(\rho_i)_{i=1}^{d_e(G)})\), where \(d_e(G)\in\{1,2\}\) and the list contains all returned \(\operatorname{FASTP}\) expressions; when \(d_e(G)=\infty\), return \((\operatorname{tree},\infty)\). If \(r>0\), construct the acyclic covariance parametrization in source coordinates, form its Jacobian and the Jacobian augmented by the row of \(\lambda_e\), and compute their generic ranks by independently randomized exact source specializations. When the ranks agree, return \((\operatorname{algebraic},\mathcal J_{G,e},2^{\min\{|D|-n+2,\binom{n-2}{2}\}})\); when the augmented rank is larger, return \((\infty,\mathcal N_{G,e})\). The positive-excess algebraic branch reports only a rank transcript and the size-sensitive universal degree upper bound and does not compute \(d_e(G)\), \(p_e\), \(\mathcal Q_{G,e}\), or \(h_{G,e}\). The tree branch does not claim to supply \(\mathcal Q_{G,e}\), \(h_{G,e}\), or the conditional source-prime-chart certificate.

obligation.what_is_open: Determine the exact value of \(D_k(n)\) for every positive \(k\) with \(n\geq6\) and \(n<2k+4\), construct attaining graph-query families, and prove that one original directed coefficient separates the generic branches.
obligation.obstruction: The established size-sensitive orientation coefficient is only an upper bound. No frozen or newly proved result realizes its extremizer throughout the remaining strip after forced covariance relations, exact \(S_G\)-localization, affine dehomogenization, and projective-infinity losses are imposed.
obligation.attempted: I combined the size-sensitive universal orientation ceiling, the one-sink equality region, the inherited lower envelope, the exact tree boundary, small-block coefficient maxima, the published cubic transfer, and the exact rational quartic. These close every case through five vertices but do not construct or exclude extremizers at six or more vertices in the remaining strip.
obligation.partial_result:
The universal projection-aware upper bound, the large-size equality, the inherited lower envelope, and the exact small-size table give, for \(n\geq4\),
\[
2^{\min\{k+1,\lfloor(n-2)/2\rfloor\}}
\leq D_k(n)
\leq2^{\min\{k+1,\binom{n-2}{2}\}}.
\]
They also give
\[
D_0(2)=1,\qquad D_k(3)=1,\qquad D_k(4)=2,
\]
and
\[
D_0(5)=2,\qquad D_1(5)=3,\qquad D_k(5)=4\quad(k\geq2).
\]
Moreover \(D_k(n)=2^{k+1}\) whenever \(n\geq2k+4\). Thus the only unresolved pairs have \(k>0\), \(n\geq6\), and \(n<2k+4\); the size-sensitive upper envelope is not asserted to be attained there.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The open question's obligation metadata must display the same proved two-sided envelope as its narrowed statement.

proposed.statement: Does there exist, in \(\mathsf{ArithmeticModel}\), a chart-free randomized algorithm which, for every \((G,T,e)\in\mathcal G_{n,k}\) with \(d_e(G)<\infty\), constructs the exact tuple \((d_e(G),p_e,\mathcal Q_{G,e},h_{G,e})\) with time and certificate length \(n^{C(k+1)}\operatorname{poly}(\log(1/\delta))\) and symbolic error probability at most \(\delta\)? Constructing valid source-prime chart packages with \(s\leq n^b\) and \(\mathfrak d\leq n^{b(k+1)}\) would suffice by \(\mathrm{thm:conditional\mbox{-}geometric\mbox{-}resolution}\), but no equivalence with bounded chart construction is claimed.
proposed.justification: The unconditional finite-output guarantee is the remaining algorithmic commitment after the valid algebraicity tag is separated from chart-dependent elimination.
proposed.gap: The quadratic core does not provide a reduced local presentation, a source-nonzero Jacobian minor, source-component selection, or bounded descent over the implicitly presented covariance field.
proposed.consumer: Resolving this question positively would remove the chart input from the exact higher-degree fasttreeid workflow.

obligation.what_is_open: Construct, from the graph input alone, bounded source-prime charts or a different chart-free representation that selects the source-induced component over \(K_G\), descends its queried-coordinate eliminant to \(K_G[t]\), and certifies every recorded pole, projective-infinity, squarefreeness, specialization, and real-lifting condition within the stated fixed-parameter bound.
obligation.obstruction: The frozen quadratic core preserves the queried projection only extensionally. It supplies neither generators of the embedded source prime nor a source-nonzero Jacobian minor, a reduced local regular sequence, or bounded descent data over the implicitly presented covariance field. The two frozen geometric-resolution results begin after equations and the relevant inequation have been supplied; they do not distinguish the source-induced component from other components of the recorded core. Consequently, applying them to the union can introduce extraneous queried values, whereas saturating recorded source-coordinate divisors can delete genuine zero-over-zero branches. The existing premises therefore prove sufficiency of bounded valid charts but neither construct them nor give a generic-class impossibility witness for every alternative chart-free algorithm, so an honest positive or negative resolution is unavailable.
obligation.attempted: I applied the frozen lifting-fiber decomposition to all recorded quadratic-core strata, but it decomposes the presented union without identifying which component is induced by source evaluation. I then considered saturating by every recorded denominator, but that conflicts with incidence localization because legitimate branches may lie on zero-over-zero divisor strata. Finally, I considered generic slicing and multiplication matrices after the unconditional Jacobian tag; these recover the minimal polynomial only after a correct source-prime chart and descent data are supplied, which is precisely the missing input.
obligation.partial_result:
The strongest conclusion derivable from the frozen core is the following conditional reduction. Fix \((G,T,e)\in\mathcal G_{n,k}\) with \(d_e(G)<\infty\). The already established theorem \(\mathrm{thm:conditional\mbox{-}geometric\mbox{-}resolution}\) states that, if a valid source-prime chart package \(\mathfrak C_{G,e}\) is supplied for every source-consistent recorded stratum, then a randomized localized geometric-resolution algorithm returns
\[
\bigl(d_e(G),p_e,\mathcal Q_{G,e},h_{G,e}\bigr)
\]
with symbolic error probability at most \(\delta\), arithmetic time and certificate length at most
\[
(n+s)^{a(k+1)}\mathfrak d^{a}\operatorname{poly}\!\left(\log(1/\delta)\right),
\]
where \(s=s(\mathfrak C_{G,e})\) and \(\mathfrak d=\mathfrak d(\mathfrak C_{G,e})\). In particular, if a universal \(b>0\) satisfies
\[
s\leq n^b
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\mathfrak d\leq n^{b(k+1)},
\]
then
\[
(n+s)^{a(k+1)}\mathfrak d^{a}
\leq
(n+n^b)^{a(k+1)}n^{ab(k+1)}
\leq
2^{a(k+1)}n^{a\max\{1,b\}(k+1)+ab(k+1)}.
\]
Because \(n\geq2\), the last expression is at most \(n^{C(k+1)}\) for a universal constant \(C\) depending only on \(a\) and \(b\). Thus bounded valid-chart construction is sufficient for the requested fixed-parameter exact finite output.

Unconditionally, the already established theorem \(\mathrm{thm:fpt\mbox{-}minimal\mbox{-}polynomial}\) returns the correct algebraic-versus-transcendental tag. On the algebraic branch it certifies
\[
d_e(G)\leq2^{\min\{|D|-n+2,\binom{n-2}{2}\}}
\leq2^{\min\{k+1,\binom{n-2}{2}\}},
\]
but, as its statement explicitly records, it does not compute \(d_e(G)\), \(p_e\), \(\mathcal Q_{G,e}\), or \(h_{G,e}\). Hence the frozen core proves the chart-conditional implication and the unconditional tag, but it does not prove the requested chart-free construction.

Exact equality \(D_k(n)=2^{k+1}\) holds when \(n\geq2k+4\), and the exact table is \(D_0(2)=1\), \(D_k(3)=1\), \(D_k(4)=2\), \(D_0(5)=2\), \(D_1(5)=3\), and \(D_k(5)=4\) for \(k\geq2\). prose_updates.tldr: Adding parents to a supplied rooted tree creates finite ambiguity measured here by the single-coordinate complex degree \(D_k(n)\), not by whole-fiber cardinality or real root count. For \(n\geq4\), the paper proves the honest two-sided envelope \(2^{\min\{k+1,\lfloor(n-2)/2\rfloor\}}\leq D_k(n)\leq2^{\min\{k+1,\binom{n-2}{2}\}}\), together with \(D_k(n)=2^{k+1}\) for \(n\geq2k+4\) and the exact frontier for every \(n\leq5\). The upper envelope is not claimed attained in the only unresolved region, \(k>0\), \(n\geq6\), and \(n<2k+4\). Because \(\mathcal G_{n,0}\) is exactly the published tree class, the unconditional dispatcher retains its complete \(1/2/\infty\) classification and finite expressions at zero excess; positive excess currently receives an exact algebraic-versus-transcendental Jacobian tag and the size-sensitive degree ceiling. Exact positive-excess polynomials, exceptional sets, real lifting, and regular inference are proved on the supplied-valid-chart and successful-output domain of the conditional geometric-resolution theorem.

project_justification.fill: The paper proves the projection-aware degree upper bound and the two-sided envelope \(2^{\min\{k+1,\lfloor(n-2)/2\rfloor\}}\leq D_k(n)\leq2^{\min\{k+1,\binom{n-2}{2}\}}\) for \(n\geq4\), the large-size equality, the inherited all-size lower envelope, and the exact \(n\leq5\) coordinate-degree frontier. It isolates the remaining positive-\(k\), \(n\geq6\) small-size frontier in \(\mathrm{oeq:sharp\mbox{-}size\mbox{-}frontier}\) without claiming that the upper cap is attained there. It supplies an unconditional randomized Jacobian-rank tag, retains the complete published tree-case output at \(k=0\), and proves a conditional geometric-resolution theorem with explicit straight-line-program and intermediate-degree dependence. Exceptional-set, real-lifting, and regular-inference results hold only on the supplied-valid-chart and successful-output domain.

prose_updates.related_work: Van der Zander, Wienöbst, Bläser, and Liśkiewicz introduced TreeID for directed-tree linear SEMs. On this same zero-excess class, Gupta and Bläser proved that each queried coefficient has generically one, two, or infinitely many values and returned the finite values as FASTPs; Briefs and Bläser accelerated that tree-only algorithm in fasttreeid. This cited zero-excess theorem is consumed only by \(\mathrm{lem:tree\mbox{-}class\mbox{-}algorithm\mbox{-}transfer}\); it does not extend to positive \(k\). Equivalently, the published tree class is exactly \(\mathcal G_{n,0}\), up to the harmless vertex-count indexing shift, and is not \(\mathcal G_{n,k}\) for positive \(k\). Foygel, Draisma, and Drton give the published five-node whole-fiber cubic used here only as the \(D_1(5)\) coordinate base case; their cubic and other small higher-degree examples are not novelty claims. Hollering, Misra, and Sturma optimize bounded-degree rational formulas, a different degree notion. Giusti, Lecerf, and Salvy compute geometric resolutions for reduced regular sequences away from an inequation (DOI 10.1006/jcom.2000.0571), and Lecerf treats arbitrary equations and inequations with complexity charged to intermediate geometric degree (DOI 10.1016/S0885-064X(03)00031-1); neither selects the embedded source component or manufactures its source-nonzero chart. The exceptional-set, real-lifting, regular-cell, root-separation, finite-set, and singleton-inference results are proved only after a valid chart and successful conditional output are supplied; they cover every retained branch without claiming discriminant-uniform inference or automatic branch selection.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: For \(k>0\), \(n\geq6\), and \(n<2k+4\), the exact frontier remains between the proved lower and upper envelopes \(2^{\min\{k+1,\lfloor(n-2)/2\rfloor\}}\) and \(2^{\min\{k+1,\binom{n-2}{2}\}}\): the orientation coefficient may lose branches through forced covariance relations, exact localization, affine dehomogenization, or projective infinity. The exhaustive five-node orbit census is a secondary regression and coordinate-census question, not a kill test for the numerical frontier, because the cubic and quartic base cases and the entire \(n\leq5\) frontier are fixed. Independently, the quadratic core does not construct a reduced local presentation of the embedded source prime or bounded rational-circuit descent over \(K_G\). On the certified event determined by a supplied valid source-prime chart, the exceptional-set theorem, real-root-lifting theorem, regular-cell lemma, derived root-separation lemma, regular finite-set inference theorem, and singleton inference proposition hold. Their chart antecedent appears in every statement; no chart-free statistical theorem is asserted. Coordinate localization is never promoted to equality of full fibers, real roots are never equated with real supported lifts, and local rank is not used to assert real uniqueness.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The paper proves the full frontier through five vertices, the all-size lower envelope, the size-sensitive upper envelope \(D_k(n)\leq2^{\min\{k+1,\binom{n-2}{2}\}}\), and the large-size equality, but not the remaining positive-excess small-size strip; the upper cap is not claimed attained there. Unconditionally, the dispatcher returns the complete published \(1/2/\infty\) classification and finite \(\operatorname{FASTP}\) expressions on \(\mathcal G_{n,0}\). For \(|D\setminus T|>0\), it returns only a randomized algebraic-versus-transcendental tag, a rank or dominance certificate, and the sharper ceiling \(d_e(G)\leq2^{\min\{|D|-n+2,\binom{n-2}{2}\}}\); it does not return \(d_e(G)\), \(p_e\), \(\mathcal Q_{G,e}\), or \(h_{G,e}\) on the algebraic branch. Given valid source-prime charts and successful output, the conditional geometric-resolution theorem returns those exact finite objects with its stated straight-line-program and intermediate-degree dependence. On precisely that same conditional domain, the six exceptional-set, real-lifting, and regular-inference results are proved. No discriminant-uniform inference, automatic branch selection, or all-singular-covariance guarantee is claimed, and positive definiteness of recovered noise follows only after a complete real supported lift by congruence.

statement_notes.justification: This gives a universal projection-aware ceiling sensitive both to excess-parent count and to the number of available child blocks.
statement_notes.gap: Existing tree-only identification theory and old higher-degree small SEM examples do not provide this single-coordinate size-and-excess bound.
statement_notes.consumer: A fixed-parameter symbolic engine can allocate elimination degree and certificate storage using the sharper of the excess and vertex-size exponents before seeing numerical covariance values.
